title: NIST WebBook: Methane gas-phase standard enthalpy of combustion
summary: The WebBook lists 4 gas-phase standard enthalpy of combustion row(s) for Methane. Reviewed rows and experimental rows are both quoted.
body: The NIST Chemistry WebBook gas-phase standard enthalpy of combustion rows for Methane (CAS 74-82-8) print: -890.7 ± 0.4 kJ/mol, method Ccb, reference Pittam and Pilcher, 1972, comment: Corresponding Δ f Hº gas = -74.48 kJ/mol (simple calculation by NIST; no Washburn corrections); ALS (experimental or compiled row) | -890.35 ± 0.30 kJ/mol, method Ccb, reference Prosen and Rossini, 1945, comment: Hf derived from Heat of Hydrogenation; Corresponding Δ f Hº gas = -74.822 kJ/mol (simple calculation by NIST; no Washburn corrections); ALS (experimental or compiled row) | -891.8 ± 1.1 kJ/mol, method Ccb, reference Roth and Banse, 1932, comment: Reanalyzed by Cox and Pilcher, 1970 , Original value = -887.3 ± 1.0 kJ/mol; Corresponding Δ f Hº gas = -73.39 kJ/mol (simple calculation by NIST; no Washburn corrections); ALS (experimental or compiled row) | -890.16 ± 0.30 kJ/mol, method Cm, reference Rossini, 1931, comment: Corresponding Δ f Hº gas = -75.010 kJ/mol (simple calculation by NIST; no Washburn corrections); ALS (experimental or compiled row). The page mixes reviewed or averaged rows with rows tied to a named experiment or compilation. A Review or AVG method is an evaluation. A Ccb method is combustion calorimetry, as the WebBook method code is linked. This card does not average the rows into a new number.
